To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MIF is a pro-inflammatory cytokine that has been shown to play an important role in carcinogenesis and that ATIII can bind to and inhibit MIF activity.

1) MIF is a pro-inflammatory cytokine that is upregulated in various cancers; 2) ATIII is a MIF binding protein that reduces the biological activity of MIF; 3) MIF-ATIII complexes are decreased in the serum of bladder cancer patients; and 4) MIF- ATIII complexes are decreased during the progression of cancer.
ATIII-MIF complex formation is a novel mechanism of MIF inactivation and that serum MIF levels are increased in patients with bladder cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of MIF inhibitors and the characterization of the biological activity of the MIF-ATIII complex.
the identification of MIF binding proteins and their role in regulating MIF bioactivity.
the development of new biomarkers of bladder cancer, as well as the identification of novel therapeutic targets for the treatment of bladder cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MIF and MIF-ATIII complex formation may be a potential biomarker for bladder cancer.
ATIII-MIF complex formation may be an important mechanism for MIF inactivation in bladder cancer patient sera.
the increase in serum levels of MIF in bladder and other cancers is not due to increased MIF production, but is rather due to a decrease in MIF binding proteins.

ATIII-MIF complex formation is decreased in bladder cancer serum.
